Today's big story: Anthropic Below Its IPO Price: Do Giants Come Back?

Reddit (RDDT) grew its revenue faster than any of its peers in a group of five companies. Its sales rose 62.2% in the four quarters to September 30, 2026. Yet its stock lost 50.8% over the year to Tuesday's close, the worst in the group. The shares fell 29.2% on October 30 alone, the day after Reddit's third-quarter results. So is Reddit priced right for what it delivers?

Does Reddit's price match its growth against its peers?

On the group's own ranks, the price looks low for the growth. Reddit trades at 17.5 times its profit over the last four quarters. That figure is the price to earnings ratio, or P/E. Income outside the business lifted that profit a little, as explained below. Of the four companies with a P/E rank, Reddit has the second highest. Meta Platforms has the highest, at 20 times.

No peer has both a higher P/E and faster growth than Reddit. Alphabet and Match Group sit below it on both. Alphabet's low P/E owes much to income outside its business. Its net income of $236 billion was well above its operating income of $157 billion. In the June quarter alone, its net income was about 2.8 times its operating income. Pinterest is left out of the P/E rank because it lost money in two recent quarters.

Share prices have not followed growth. Meta grew less than half as fast as Reddit, yet its shares lost just 0.41% over the same year, dividends included.

Reddit shares fell 50.8% in a year while its sales rose 62.2%. Owners who sat through that fall got no payout from the stock to soften it. Margin may explain part of Meta's higher P/E. Operating margin is the share of sales left after the costs of running the business. Over the four quarters, Meta's was 32.9%. Reddit's was 29.4%, fourth of five. But Meta's margin fell to about 20% in the September quarter, below Reddit's 29.2%.

title: What Should Reddit Stock Owners Watch Now?
detail:
What Should Reddit Stock Owners Watch Now?

Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Nvidia Added $954 Billion In A Day. Is Jensen Huang Too Big To Fire?

Reddit is still growing fast. Its revenue rose 53% in the three months to September, against the same months a year earlier. The stock tells a different story. It closed at $88.76 on Monday, November 23. That is 65.7% below its highest close of $258.93 on January 13.

Holders have one real worry, in our view. It does not start inside Reddit's own app. It starts with how people find the site in the first place. Management raised it itself, and it could cut Reddit's daily users. So where are Reddit's visitors going?

What Is Happening To Reddit's Search Traffic?

Google is sending fewer people to Reddit. A search referral is a visit that starts with a search on Google or another engine. On its October 29 call, management said "our search referral traffic was down meaningfully in Q3." It tied the drop to Google's rollout of "AI Mode."

The slide went on into October. Management said search traffic "dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week." If that continued, it said, daily users "could fall in Q4 by a low double-digit percentage from our current base of 130 million DAUqs." DAUq is Reddit's count of daily active unique visitors.

The shares fell 29.2% on Friday, October 30, the day after the call. Measured close to close, that was the stock's largest one-day move of the past year.

Reddit lost 29.2% in one day, and its owners get no cash from the company while they wait for a rebound. If your savings have to keep covering your bills, a fall like that in one stock can leave you selling at the worst time. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

How Much Of Reddit's Business Does It Touch?

Search visitors see the ads that bring in nearly all of Reddit's sales. Management said "Q3 revenue was $895 million" and "advertising revenue was $847 million." Our data does not split Reddit's sales into reported segments, and the call does not say how much of that ad money comes from search visitors.

Search visitors are not Reddit's most valuable users, though. Management said "80% of the monetization of Reddit happens within our app and logged-in cohort." Many search visitors land on the mobile website instead. Management said it will keep working to move them to the app.

Growth has slowed for three quarters in a row. The table shows total company revenue in each quarter and its growth against the same quarter a year earlier.

Anthropic began trading on Thursday, Nov 19. It sold its shares at $83 and closed its first day at $97.17, up 17.1%. On Friday, Nov 20, it closed at $88.91. That was 8.5% below Thursday's close and still 7.1% above the offer price.

Did Friday's slide make the stock cheap? We looked at what the last ten giant US listings did after a day like Friday.

Did Friday change the multiple? Yes, by about three points. The multiple here is market value divided by sales over the last four quarters. Anthropic booked $35.3 billion of revenue in those four quarters. The final prospectus lists 13.22 billion shares. At Thursday's close, that made Anthropic worth about $1.28 trillion, about 36 times sales. At Friday's $88.91, it is worth about $1.18 trillion, or 33 times.

About $109 billion of market value came off Thursday's close in one trading day. That is about three years of Anthropic's sales at the pace of the last four quarters. Whether 33 times sales holds up depends on how long the growth lasts. We looked at that question in Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Anthropic was not alone. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) fell 2.0% on Thursday and 3.6% on Friday. The Nasdaq-100 fund (QQQ) fell 2.2% and 5.7%. SpaceX, June's giant listing, fell 7.7% on Friday. Anthropic's first buyers paid up just as the market turned down.

At 33 times sales, some investors may want Anthropic at a lower price. Waiting for it means cash set aside for a while. The right price can take months. Meanwhile, the Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3x the S&P 500's, from 50 stocks with at least 10 straight years of dividends. See if it fits.

Is A Second-Day Fall Unusual?

No. Seven of ten fell. We went back to the ten giant US listings in our earlier study, from Google in 2004 to SpaceX in June. We measured each one's second trading day. Reddit's latest quarter showed solid revenue and advertising growth, alongside management warnings that search referral traffic is declining faster, which could affect future user activity and the monetization mix.

The company is pushing AI powered ads, shopping tools, and tighter control over third party AI access as it tries to offset weaker search driven traffic with more direct engagement and on platform commerce.

We will examine how Reddit's investment narrative holds up as management confronts accelerating search referral declines and leans harder into AI driven monetization.

Scan how Reddit's AI heavy ad pivot compares with other platforms leaning on machine learning by filtering for 43 profitable AI stocks that aren't just burning cash that already back big promises with real profits.

Reddit Investment Narrative Recap

To own Reddit, you need to believe the platform can convert deep community intent into durable advertising and commerce revenue even as search referrals fade. According to John_Eric, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key upside comes from high gross margins, strong recent earnings growth and a near debt free balance sheet that supports continued product investment.

The near term catalyst now is whether AI driven ads and shopping tools can keep revenue growth resilient while daily users face pressure from weaker Google referrals. The biggest risk is that search driven declines hurt engagement faster than on platform monetization ramps, which could keep volatility and execution scrutiny high.

The most relevant update is Reddit's push into AI powered product discovery and shopping, including tests that surface ads near search style queries and summarize community reviews. This directly targets the referral problem by trying to keep users researching and buying inside Reddit instead of bouncing out to external sites.

If these tools gain traction, they could support ad pricing, attract more retail and B2B marketers and reduce reliance on outside search engines over time. Execution risk is real, especially with RDDT's share price having fallen sharply in recent months and sentiment already cautious, but successful adoption would speak directly to the core traffic and monetization catalyst.

John_Eric's narrative arrives at a fair value of $195.00 for Reddit by applying a discounted cash flow framework that assumes revenue expands at 15.7% a year and the business eventually settles at a future profit margin of 31.3%, reflecting his view of Reddit's long run earnings power.

Reddit Inc. (RDDT) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Shares of this company have returned -38.6% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -4.3% change. The Zacks Internet - Software industry, to which Reddit Inc. belongs, has lost 10% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

Reddit Inc. is expected to post earnings of $1.76 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +41.9%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +1.3%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $5.42 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +106.9%. This estimate has changed +2.9% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $6.73 indicates a change of +24.2% from what Reddit Inc. is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -2.9%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Reddit (RDDT) stock closed at $94.48 on November 17, 2026, down 39.5% from its October 16 close. A drop that steep tempts anyone who liked the company at a higher price. The shares might be a bargain on a business that is still growing. Or they could be a warning that the underlying story has changed. The steepest single-day decline arrived right after Reddit reported its fiscal Q3 2026 results on October 29. So what did management tell investors on that call?

What Did Reddit Tell Investors On Its Q3 Call?

Search referral traffic, the visitors search engines send to Reddit, fell meaningfully in the third quarter, management said on the call. The decline sped up late in the quarter, management said. Management said the slide continued into early October. At that rate, it said, daily users could fall from 130 million by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter. The shares lost 29.2% on October 30, the day after the call. That marked their largest one-day fall of the past year.

Management said on the call that the drop in search traffic appears to come from Google's rollout of AI Mode. It said people still want Reddit, and Google is just not sending them there the way it used to. Management also said 80% of Reddit's monetization happens in its app and among logged-in users. So the search warning on the call was about how many people reach Reddit, not about the ads it has already sold. On the same call, management guided fourth-quarter revenue growth below the third quarter's pace.

Did Reddit's Earlier Falls Of This Size Pay Off?

Since March 2024, Reddit stock has fallen more than 40% over 30 trading days three times. The latest, on November 2, 2026, came partway through this slide. The February 2026 drop is less than a year old. So only one has a full year behind it. In the 30 trading days to March 10, 2025, the shares fell 41.2% while the S&P 500 ETF fell 8.0%. A year after that date, they were 30.0% higher.

Collecting that gain meant sitting through a further fall first. At their lowest that year, the shares closed 19.0% below the March 10 price. The highest price came 192 days after the dip, about six months later. It stood 152.3% above the dip-date price. The February 2026 drop remains too recent to judge over a year, but the shares traded 14.0% higher six months on.
